interactions.summary: The reading covers Jason's betrayal of Medea and the transition to the next pouch.
Jiang retells Jason and Medea, confirms Medea's revenge through the murder of her children, and then asks the class what kind of life would deserve drowning in excrement.

claims.claim: Jiang retells Jason and Medea as a story of upward ambition in which Jason betrays Medea by marrying a princess after Medea helped him succeed.
Jiang confirms Medea's revenge by saying she kills her two young children after the betrayal.
Jiang frames the next punishment as a riddle: what kind of life would warrant being immersed in filth forever.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns the punishment itself into a moral guessing game: what kind of life earns an eternity of drowning in excrement?
signature_moments.source_phrase: awash in shit for all of eternity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The coarse phrasing carries the disgust Dante wants and sets up the flattery interpretation cleanly.

chronology_notes.note: The packet bridges one betrayal narrative into the next fraud punishment by making the class infer the sin from the bodily image.
